title: The axial blind spot of a radial cell model: the temperature field a multi-unit model assumes, tested on the LG M50 and a 4680
description: Pre-registered comparison of the one-dimensional radial thermal model that gives each spiral unit its temperature in the multi-unit model of Yang, Cui and Tartakovsky (J. Electrochem. Soc. 173 (2026) 050520) with a resolved three-dimensional cell (anisotropic jelly roll and steel can, scikit-fem, from doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23253738), with the heat held equal. The heat comes from PyBaMM's Doyle-Fuller-Newman model with the Chen2020 parameter set at 1.25C, 2C and 3C and ambients of minus 5 C and 25 C, applied uniformly per volume; the thermal properties are those of O'Regan et al. 2022; the cooling is the paper's h = 400 W/(m2 K). The cells are an LG M50 21700 (45 units) and a 4680 with the same properties (111 units). The predictions were committed and pushed to GitHub (commit b92f9a8) before any three-dimensional field was computed. The paper's radial model carries no heat along the cell's axis, which in three dimensions means insulated ends. Under that condition the resolved cell supports it: at 2C and minus 5 C every unit lies within 0.29 K of its radial temperature in the M50 and within 1.2 K in the 4680. With the ends cooled at the same h, the axial difference along the core that the radial model cannot see is 37 % of the radial core-to-surface difference in the M50 (1.28 of 3.45 K) and 32 % in the 4680 (3.44 of 10.61 K), at every rate and ambient run. The radial model then puts every unit too warm, by 0.48 to 1.59 K in the M50 (mean 1.19 K) and by 1.9 to 11.3 K in the 4680 (mean 8.0 K), and overstates the unit-to-unit spread by 34 to 36 % in the M50 and 78 to 101 % in the 4680 over the six rates and ambients. At 2C and minus 5 C the cooled ends remove 19 % of the heat in the M50 and 38 % in the 4680. These are temperature offsets, not energy errors: the paper's surrogate would turn them into current and energy differences, which this study does not compute. Three of the five Stage 1 predictions held. Stage 2 (v1.1.0), with its own predictions committed and pushed before any Stage 2 computation (commit 0cb04c3; nine of ten held), settles the gap to the paper and adds a remedy. The paper's ref. 33 (J. Power Sources 664 (2026) 238948) fits its thermal values to one 1C discharge of the same cell: 0.62 W/(m K) across the layers and 3.44 MJ/(m3 K), against O'Regan's 1.23 and 2.48. With them this radial model's unit differences in the M50 rise by a factor of 1.9, which takes the factor to the paper from 1.7 to 2.2 to 0.88 to 1.13 at 25 C and from 3.5 to 3.6 to 1.87 to 1.91 at 2C and minus 5 C (the paper's own end of discharge). Ref. 33's electrochemical set, run in PyBaMM, ends the 2C, minus 5 C discharge at 1.51 A h, where the paper's ends, with 1.38 to 1.40 times Chen2020's heat; with its properties and heat the remaining factor is 0.82 to 0.85 at 25 C and 1.25 to 1.33 at minus 5 C. A one-term end correction, derived and not fitted, adds the sink beta (T minus T_amb) to the radial equation, with beta = 2 h_e / L and 1/h_e = 1/h + L/(6 k_z). With the ends cooled at h = 400 it takes the mean unit offset from 1.19 to 0.10 K in the M50 and from 7.96 to 0.21 K in the 4680 and the spread overstatement from 36 and 98 % to 5 and 3 %, matches the resolved share of heat through the ends within 0.5 percentage points and the axial difference at the core within 2 %, and keeps the offset at 0.16 K at h = 25. Stage 3 (v1.2.0), with predictions committed and pushed before any test run (commit 7060663; five of seven held), tests the core-temperature estimator of ref. 33 against the resolved cell: an ensemble Kalman filter that assimilates the surface temperature and the terminal voltage and learns the forecast's error, in the thermal equation a heat source per layer. Here the forecast is the radial model with the resolved cell's heat and properties, and the reading is the resolved cell's mid-length surface temperature every 20 s with 0.1 K noise (the voltage has no counterpart here), with 3000 members as in ref. 33; the error's noise, which ref. 33 does not give, is bracketed at 0.1, 1 and 10 times a reference level. With the ends insulated the estimator stays within 0.14 K of the resolved core on average. With them cooled at 2C and minus 5 C it leaves 1.14 of the forecast's 1.18 K end-of-discharge miss in the M50 and 9.7 of 10.2 K in the 4680 (0.48 and 5.9 K at ten times the level). In the cooled M50 cases its learned error averages 1.4 to 1.7 % of the end correction's sink (36 to 44 % at ten times the level), and on the end-corrected forecast the same estimator's mean error is 0.04 to 0.13 K (0.24 K in the 4680). Checks: with the can on the side only, the resolved cell matches the radial model within 0.15 %; energy closes to 2e-12; one mesh refinement changes the core-to-surface difference by 0.09 %; an independent axisymmetric recomputation agrees within 0.15 %; the corrected model reduces exactly to the radial model without the sink and matches its modified Bessel steady solution. Contents: the code (Python with NumPy, SciPy, scikit-fem, pyamg, matplotlib and PyBaMM), the decisions log, the three sets of predictions, the heat inputs, the results in JSON and CSV, the figures, the note, the verification files, an independent recomputation, an independent audit report and the independent read of Stage 3.
